perturbed_solution: Putting the first equation in slope-intercept form gives $y = 3x - a$ which means this line has a slope of 3.  Similarly the second equation gives $y = (a + 6)x + 1,$ meaning it has a slope of $a + 6$.  Since the two lines are parallel they have equal slopes: $3 = a + 6 \Rightarrow a =  oxed{-9}$.

errors.original_text: Putting the first equation in slope-intercept form gives $y = 3x + a$
errors.injected_text: Putting the first equation in slope-intercept form gives $y = 3x - a$
errors.rationale: The constant term should be $+a$, not $-a$. From $2y - 2a = 6x$, we get $2y = 6x + 2a$, so $y = 3x + a$. Changing it to $-a$ is a sign error in isolating the constant.
From $y + 1 = (a + 6)x$, subtracting 1 from both sides gives $y = (a + 6)x - 1$, not $+1$. This is a sign error when moving the constant to the right side.
Solving $3 = a + 6$ gives $a = 3 - 6 = -3$, not $-9$. This is an arithmetic error in the subtraction step, possibly treating the operation as addition instead.
